title: Denominator ideals of regular meromorphic sections have nowhere-dense cokernels
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $K_X$ for the sheaf of meromorphic functions (the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal S(U)^{-1}\mathcal O_X(U)$, $\mathcal S(U)$ the sections whose stalks are non-zero-divisors at every point of $U$) and $K_X(\mathcal L):=K_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L$, which contains $\mathcal L$. Let $s\in\Gamma(X,K_X(\mathcal L))$ be a regular meromorphic section, i.e. the map $K_X\to K_X(\mathcal L)$, $1\mapsto s$, is injective, and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be the subsheaf with $\mathcal I(V)=\{f\in\mathcal O_X(V)\mid fs\in\mathcal L(V)\}$. Then: (1) every point of $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with a trivialization $\mathcal L|_U\cong\mathcal O_U$ under which $s|_U$ is the image of $a/b$ with $a,b\in A$ both non-zero-divisors of $A$, and $\mathcal I(U)=\{x\in A\mid x(a/b)\in A\}$ (computed in the total ring of fractions of $A$); (2) $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals; (3) the maps $1:\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_X$ and $s:\mathcal I\to\mathcal L$ are injective, and their cokernels $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal L/s(\mathcal I)$ are supported on closed nowhere-dense subsets of $X$.

proof.text: The assertion is local on X. Fix x in X and an affine open Spec(A) containing x on which L is trivial; identify L with O_X there, so K_X(L) becomes K_X and s a section of K_X. By the definition of K_X as the sheafification of U -> S(U)^{-1}O_X(U) (Stacks Tag 01X2), a section of K_X is locally a section of the presheaf, so after shrinking to a principal affine open U = Spec(A) around x, s|_U is the image of a/b with a in A and b in S(U). Every element of S(U) is a non-zero-divisor on O_X(U) = A (its germs are non-zero-divisors at every point, and an element of A vanishing in every local ring is zero); conversely a non-zero-divisor of A stays one in every localization, so S(U) is the set of non-zero-divisors of A and the presheaf value is the total ring of fractions Q(A). As remarked after Tag 01X2, O_X -> K_X is injective. Regularity (Tag 02OX) says K_X -> K_X(L), 1 -> s, is injective; if y in A has ya = 0 then y s|_U = (ya)/b = 0, so the image of y in K_X(U) is 0 and y = 0. Hence a is a non-zero-divisor of A as well. Finally, for y in A, y s|_U lies in L(U) = A exactly when the image of ya/b in K_X(U) is the image of some z in A; then ya - bz maps to zero in K_X(U), so ya = bz by injectivity of O_X -> K_X, i.e. y(a/b) = z in Q(A). Thus I(U) = {y in A | y(a/b) in A} computed in Q(A), which is clause (1).

proof.text: For every f in A, the denominator ideal satisfies I_f = {x in A_f | x(a/b) belongs to A_f}. Indeed, if c/f^n lies in A_f and its product with a/b lies in A_f, clearing a power of f gives f^m c(a/b) in A, hence c/f^n lies in I_f; the reverse inclusion follows by localization. Thus the affine module associated to I has exactly the prescribed sections on every principal open, so I is quasi-coherent, and it is an ideal because the defining condition is closed under addition and multiplication by A.

proof.text: The inclusion I into O_X is injective by construction, and multiplication by the regular section s is injective because I is contained in O_X, which injects into K_X (Tag 01X2), and K_X to K_X(L), 1 mapping to s, is injective (Tag 02OX). In the affine trivialization of step 1, b belongs to I since b(a/b) = a lies in A, so V(I) is contained in V(b); also s(b) = a belongs to s(I), so the support of the second cokernel is contained in V(a). Since a and b are non-zero-divisors, the existing principal-open density lemma says D(a) and D(b) are dense; therefore V(a) and V(b) are closed nowhere-dense. The two cokernels are consequently supported on closed nowhere-dense subsets, and these local conclusions glue over X.
